# Chih-Yu Lin

::: {.hero-subtitle}
Ph.D. Candidate, National Taiwan University  
Visiting Researcher, University of Oulu
:::

I design wireless communication systems that are aware of **timeliness**, **task utility**, and **resource constraints**. My research focuses on 6G wireless networks, task-oriented semantic communication, integrated sensing and communication, Age of Information, NOMA, vehicular networks, and learning-based resource allocation.

For faculty applications, this website summarizes my research vision, publications, teaching interests, and professional experience.

## Research vision

Future wireless networks will not only deliver bits. They will support sensing, inference, control, and decision-making under strict timeliness and resource constraints. My research develops communication and resource allocation frameworks that answer three connected questions:

::: {.vision-grid}
::: {.vision-card}
### What should be transmitted?
Task-oriented semantic communication prioritizes information according to its usefulness for downstream tasks, rather than only reconstructing raw data.
:::

::: {.vision-card}
### When should information be updated?
Age of Information and deadline-aware metrics capture whether received information is still timely and valuable for the task.
:::

::: {.vision-card}
### How should wireless resources be shared?
NOMA, multicast/unicast coexistence, sensing, and learning-based optimization provide tools for coordinating spectrum, power, computation, and task requirements.
:::
:::
